items.title: How a daring escape by Iranian soccer players secured their asylum in Australia
items.description: Australian officials waited on the sidelines of the Iranian football team's final game in the Gold Coast on Sunday, signalling to players help was available if they wanted to talk. The government has granted temporary humanitarian visas to five of the athletes after they escaped from their team hotel with assistance from Australian Federal Police and requested asylum.

items.title: Live: Trump says war could be over soon, Iran says his comments are 'nonsense'
items.description: Iranian politicians and institutions have issued pledges of loyalty to the new supreme leader. Follow live.

items.title: What is a Wedgetail, the powerful aircraft Australia is sending to war?
items.description: One of Australia's most sophisticated military surveillance planes will be deployed to the Middle East, along with a crew of about 85 defence personnel to operate it.

items.title: 'Unprepared' to defend against Iranian drones, US calls on Ukraine for help
items.description: Ukraine is called upon to provide drone defence expertise to the US and Gulf states as the region struggles to counter swarms of Iranian attack drones.

items.title: In the early hours of the Iran war, Indonesia's president made a telling offer
items.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's big ambitions on the world stage and at home have alarmed his critics.

items.title: Live: ASX rises after heavy sell-off as oil prices moderate
items.description: The Australian market is tracking higher after Wall Street's overnight rise. The ASX 200 is up 1.5 per cent, regaining some of yesterday's losses, spurred by concerns about the impact of the Middle East war. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Dubai's influencers stopped talking about war and started a 'cringe' trend
items.description: As missiles and drones began lighting up the sky over Dubai, many of the city's social media personalities started posting about it. Then the government stepped in.

items.title: Teenager appeals 16-year sentence for murder of Vyleen White
items.description: The 17-year-old boy, who cannot legally be named, pleaded guilty to Vyleen White's murder and several other offences last year.

items.title: Labor to pass super tax changes with support of Greens
items.description: The legislation comes as speculation builds that the federal government will pursue more ambitious tax changes in the May budget.

items.title: Court rules 'no reasonable basis' for $ 2.3m lawsuit against SA premier
items.description: South Australia's Supreme Court has thrown out former MP Annabel Digance's $2.3 million lawsuit against the state and Premier Peter Malinauskas, but found it was still open for her to pursue complaints about the conduct of SA Police.

items.title: Family of 14yo says Aidan Becker ‘risked his life to save our son’
items.description: The family of a 14-year-old boy allegedly attacked in Mernda last week said Aidan Becker, who was fatally stabbed trying to protect the teenager, showed "extraordinary courage and compassion in risking his life to save our son".

items.title: Live: Bundaberg residents told to 'leave immediately' as floodwaters rise, bridges to shut
items.description: A major flood is threatening Bundaberg after days of rain spilled dams and set rivers on the rise across Queensland.

items.title: Boil water alert issued for Darwin after pumping failure at main drinking supply
items.description: The NT health department has issued a boil water alert for Darwin, after problems with the pump station at Darwin River Dam caused by flash flooding.

items.title: Minns can't say when sinkhole-plagued M6 will open, legal action possible
items.description: NSW Premier Chris Minns said he does not know if the troubled M6 motorway will open while he is still in power.

items.title: Five things I do (as a therapist) when anxiety takes over
items.description: No-one is harder on me than me. Anxiety thrives on this. Along the way, I've built a toolkit that helps me regulate, reconnect and come back to myself.

items.title: ABC Shakespeare quiz: How well doest thou know his characters and quotes?
items.description: A quiz by any other word would smell as sweet, or something, so have a crack at our 10 questions on the works of William Shakespeare.

items.title: American western fashion is back. Here's how the trend made it to our city streets
items.description: From streetwear to festival fits, country fashion has become mainstream in Australian cities and heritage brands are reaping the benefits.

items.title: Government warned now-closed 'horse and cart' Convict Bridge unfit for modern traffic
items.description: The Blue Mountains community warned the NSW government the Great Western Highway's historic Convict Bridge could not withstand modern day traffic prior to its closure last week.

items.title: Queensland workplace safety regulator 'captured' by CFMEU, inquiry hears
items.description: Senior counsel assisting Patrick Wheelahan alleges Workplace Health and Safety Queensland became "improperly dominated" by the interests of the CFMEU.

items.title: Plan for thousands of new homes at 'one of Sydney's most vibrant areas'
items.description: The NSW government on Tuesday unveiled plans to rezone the 113-hectare Burwood North precinct, positioning it as a residential hub between Sydney's CBD and Parramatta.

items.title: Officials intercept 150,000 melatonin units at border, amid broader crackdown
items.description: Australian Border Force officials have intercepted more than 150,000 units of melatonin in four months, after authorities warned they would crack down on unregulated products.

items.title: Will this year's flu vaccine protect against the fast-moving Super-K strain?
items.description: Experts say they are feeling "nervous" as Australia approached this year's flu season, with a new, fast-moving strain of influenza dubbed "Super-K" circulating as vaccine uptake dwindles.

items.title: Forwarded email a rare public glimpse into the cunning world of political spin
items.description: It is common for media advisors to provide reporters with background information in an effort to shape the way a story is reported, but the practice backfired spectacularly when the SA government shared an email from the wrong patient.

items.title: As Alex Johnston approaches eternity, rugby league must brace itself
items.description: As Alex Johnston moves to the edge of forever in his chase of the all-time try-scoring record, rugby league must brace itself for a chance that only comes around once or twice a century.

items.title: Rainforest river cruise boat found on Great Barrier Reef after flash flood
items.description: Operators in the world heritage Daintree Rainforest are anxious about lost business after tour boats and ferries were damaged in floods ahead of the Easter holidays.
